tasks.short: Read current professional literature and judge its relevance to training practice.

steps.what: Search publication services for current articles and books.
Scan abstracts and introductions to choose what deserves deeper reading.

loop.input: Licensed article metadata, abstracts and the specialist's topic list.
loop.output: Suggested reading shortlist with source identifiers, relevance reasons and evidence-type labels.
loop.check: Require every item to match retrieved metadata; verify supporting abstract passages and sample excluded items.
loop.stop: One pass over a capped weekly batch and one repair; missing abstracts enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keywords miss synonymous topics and cannot reliably distinguish relevant research from adjacent commentary.

steps.what: Read selected sources and assess methods, limitations and practical implications.
Record useful findings, references and questions for future training design.

tasks.design: Retrieve authorised metadata from publication services in {OTHER}, remove duplicates and prepare a bounded relevance shortlist in {DOCS}. The specialist reads selected sources and records original judgements in a configured evidence log, with references populated automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Publication access was fragmented, and searching and recording references took effort. Deep reading was never simply an information retrieval problem.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata connectors, duplicate detection and bounded abstract classification reduce preparation; configured records remove repeated reference entry.
tasks.still_hard: Critical appraisal and durable professional learning require attention. Licensing limits retrieval, and automated relevance filtering can hide useful dissenting evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding why a finding may fail in a particular workplace and connecting it to lived teaching experience.

ambition.what: A monthly evidence briefing for line managers on one practical learning question.

tasks.altitude: The week retains substantial reading, with less searching and reference administration. The specialist can recommend better-supported experiments; authority to change company policy remains unchanged.

reach.task: Assess evidence before changing employee development policy.
reach.learn: Critical appraisal, study applicability and how to define a reversible policy pilot.

evidence.claim: Metadata retrieval and duplicate detection are deterministic; abstract relevance assessment can use bounded text classification.
Reading and critical appraisal are part of professional development rather than removable administration.
The documented Deloitte report refund illustrates the need to verify sources; it does not establish reliable literature appraisal.

assumptions: The baseline concerns reading for professional competence rather than producing a formal systematic review.
{OTHER} denotes publication search services.
The document-heavy, low-drudgery prior is retained; deep reading remains human.
Retrieval respects source licences and uses existing access.
No employee records are needed; GDPR still applies to any stored user preferences or activity records.
Build ranges cover a small authorised source set and exclude new publication subscriptions.
unknowns: Current publication access, subscriptions and permitted retrieval methods.
Languages, specialist topics and weekly publication volume.
Whether an existing evidence log or reference process already meets the need.
Storage and retention requirements for reading preferences and activity.
research_questions: How often does the shortlist exclude an article the specialist later considers important?
Which sources provide usable metadata and abstracts under existing licences?
new_work: Review shortlist relevance and sample exclusions.
Maintain source connectors and topic preferences.
Handle unavailable abstracts and changed access rights.
Record conflicting evidence and uncertainties.
Prepare and verify the optional monthly briefing.
tasks.statement: Keep up with developments in area of expertise by reading current journals, books, or magazine articles.

tasks.short: Deliver training through demonstrations, exercises, discussions and guided practice.

steps.what: Review course objectives, participant needs and previous learning results in the {LMS}.
Adapt the session plan and exercises using the course pack in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved course pack, session requirements and exercise templates.
loop.output: Session plan with source-linked examples and exercises.
loop.check: Check source references, objective coverage and duration; the training specialist approves adaptations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; flag unsupported content and fall back to approved exercises.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble the plan, but adapting examples to participant questions requires language generation.

steps.what: Confirm session resources, participant access and invitations through the {LMS} and {CALENDAR}.
Present concepts, demonstrate techniques and answer participants' questions.
Facilitate practice, role play and discussion; give feedback and adjust pace.
Assess practice against learning criteria and record feedback in {DOCS}.
Enter attendance and approved learning results in the {LMS}.

tasks.design: Configure the {LMS} to show cohort needs, manage session bookings through {CALENDAR}, and capture attendance and trainer-entered results once. A template generator with a bounded drafting loop prepares session plans from approved material in {DOCS}; the training specialist approves adaptations and leads teaching, practice and assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course files and cohort records were separate. Preparing suitable examples still required the trainer's time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking and attendance functions handle administration. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting templates and records; bounded drafting can adapt approved examples.
tasks.still_hard: Facilitation, accessibility needs and judging practical competence remain demanding. In-person attendance still needs a reliable capture method.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer notices confusion, protects psychological safety and gives feedback suited to the person.

ambition.what: A facilitated difficult-conversation practice clinic for first-time managers.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less session assembly and administration, with more time for coached practice. The specialist chooses exercises and pacing within approved learning objectives; formal employment decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Turn recurring onboarding questions into practice scenarios.
reach.learn: Onboarding milestones and the boundary between learning feedback and personnel records.

reach.task: Resolve missing attendance and completion records.
reach.learn: Attendance evidence, correction procedures and access permissions.

evidence.claim: Session booking, attendance capture and template assembly can use configuration and deterministic rules.
Source-based drafting can reduce preparation effort but does not establish instructional quality.
The digest identifies workplace emotion recognition as prohibited; this design uses trainer observations without automated emotion inference.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured findings.
Sessions are mainly facilitated in person, with some virtual delivery; the steps give live teaching most of the time.
The {LMS} supports booking and attendance configuration.
Booking automation follows an approved session schedule.
Estimates cover one course family and existing systems.
Access and consultation ranges include GDPR review and employee consultation where national rules require it; elapsed waits may be longer.
unknowns: Available {LMS} booking, attendance and reporting functions.
How attendance is evidenced for in-person and virtual sessions.
Which assessments affect certification, job allocation or employment decisions.
Applicable national rules and existing employee consultation agreements.
research_questions: Which existing configuration can remove duplicate preparation and attendance entry?
Do adapted exercises improve practice outcomes compared with current exercises?
new_work: Review adapted examples before delivery.
Resolve booking, access and attendance exceptions.
Maintain exercise templates and approved source versions.
Check that learning observations do not become unintended employee monitoring.
tasks.statement: Present information with a variety of instructional techniques or formats, such as role playing, simulations, team exercises, group discussions, videos, or lectures.

tasks.short: Schedule classes around instructor availability, rooms, equipment, and learner constraints.

steps.what: Review training requests, required dates, cohort sizes, and course requirements.
Check instructor calendars, room capacity, and equipment bookings.
Match classes to feasible slots in a planning workbook.
Resolve clashes and negotiate alternative dates with instructors or team leads.
Confirm the schedule and enter classes and resource bookings.
Send confirmed invitations and notify affected participants of schedule changes.

tasks.design: Use native scheduling features in the {LMS} and {CALENDAR} wherever they cover the constraints. For constraints spanning both systems, a deterministic matcher on the {DATA_PLATFORM} proposes feasible slots and lists unresolved clashes. The coordinator approves publication, after which configured flows create bookings and send invitations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Resource calendars and course requirements were held separately. The planning workbook joined them, but availability changed before bookings were confirmed.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar interfaces, structured course requirements, and ordinary constraint matching can remove most checking and copying. AI-assisted coding makes the integration cheaper to build; no model is needed to choose feasible slots.
tasks.still_hard: Availability may be stale, and some equipment has no booking calendar. Last-minute changes, operational priorities, and paid external instructor commitments still require coordination.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate when several teams need the same people or facilities and recognise which scheduling constraints can reasonably change.

ambition.what: Make a weekly cohort consolidation decision before booking rooms and instructors.

tasks.altitude: The coordinator spends the week handling conflicts and reviewing proposed schedules rather than checking calendars and copying bookings. They can propose cohort consolidation more often; budget and cancellation authority do not expand.

reach.task: Balance instructor capacity against the training plan.
reach.learn: Use utilisation, lead times, and cancellation costs to compare scheduling choices.

reach.task: Coordinate onboarding sessions for new starters.
reach.learn: Connect start dates, attendance requirements, and resource booking rules.

evidence.claim: Structured availability, capacity, and precedence constraints can be handled by deterministic matching without a language model.
Native resource booking and invitation features may replace custom scheduling code when they cover the required constraints.

assumptions: A workbook commonly joins separate calendars and course requirements; companies with integrated scheduling can configure more and build less.
Calendar access uses free/busy data where possible rather than private appointment details.
Schedule approval authorises the resulting invitations, but does not authorise new supplier fees.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates; access review includes applicable national employee consultation.
unknowns: Whether native scheduling supports all room, equipment, instructor, and cohort constraints.
Which resources have reliable booking calendars.
Calendar write permissions and support for temporary holds.
External instructor booking terms and cancellation approval limits.
Applicable consultation requirements for calendar data use.
research_questions: Can existing scheduling configuration remove the workbook entirely?
Which constraints are mandatory, and which are preferences?
Can publication recheck availability and recover safely from partial booking failures?
new_work: Maintain resource capacities, scheduling preferences, and instructor availability.
Handle infeasible requests and stale availability.
Monitor failed bookings, duplicate invitations, and calendar synchronisation.
Review cohort consolidation proposals and cancellation exceptions.
tasks.statement: Schedule classes based on availability of classrooms, equipment, or instructors.

tasks.short: Select, organise and offer programmes that help employees maintain or improve job skills.

steps.what: Discuss skill needs and practical constraints with employees and line managers.
Check existing courses, prerequisites and completion records in the {LMS}.
Design the learning pathway and identify missing course materials in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Programme brief, course metadata, approved course packs and pathway templates.
loop.output: Proposed learning pathway with course references and explicit material gaps.
loop.check: Validate course identifiers, prerequisites and availability; the specialist checks learning fit and suitability.
loop.stop: One proposal and one correction pass; unresolved gaps go to manual programme design.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules filter available courses, but connecting a free-text need to learning activities requires interpretation.

steps.what: Approve programme scope, budget and delivery arrangements.
Create programme dates, capacity and enrolment options in the {LMS}.
Send programme offers and handle employee questions through {EMAIL}.
Confirm enrolments and publish joining instructions in the {LMS}.
Check participation barriers with employees and agree support or suitable alternatives.

tasks.design: Configure the {LMS} catalogue, prerequisites, capacity, enrolment and notifications, with dates shared through {CALENDAR}. A bounded loop drafts learning pathways from approved course metadata and the programme brief in {DOCS}; the specialist checks suitability and the training and development manager approves scope and spending before offers are released.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course metadata was incomplete, while programme design and enrolment administration were mixed together. Staff availability and access barriers required direct discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment features can handle most administration. Better catalogue structure and a small drafting loop make programme preparation feasible without autonomous course allocation.
tasks.still_hard: Training may not solve a performance problem caused by workload, tools or management. Fair access, shift coverage and meaningful learning pathways still need people.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist identifies the real skill need and negotiates learning arrangements that employees can use.

ambition.what: Rotating-shift employees who cannot attend standard daytime programmes.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time publishing offers and enrolling people, and more time agreeing workable learning pathways. They manage routine enrolment within approved criteria; programme budgets and consequential employee decisions retain their existing approvers.

reach.task: Connect development requests to onboarding and role changes.
reach.learn: Role requirements and how to separate voluntary development from mandatory qualification.

reach.task: Agree training arrangements affecting shifts and employee participation.
reach.learn: National rules, collective agreements and consultation requirements for training time.

evidence.claim: Catalogue filtering, prerequisites, capacity checks and enrolment notifications can use configured rules.
A source-constrained drafting loop can propose pathways, while people assess programme suitability.
The digest identifies employment evaluation and certain worker-management uses as potentially high-risk under the EU AI Act; intended use must be assessed.
A human approval step alone does not remove the need to assess GDPR restrictions on significant automated decisions.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
This task covers programme selection and offering; course authoring and live delivery appear in the other tasks.
The {LMS} supports prerequisites, capacity and employee enrolment.
Routine enrolment uses transparent approved criteria; contested or consequential exclusions go to a person.
Automated messages use approved programme information and recipient rules.
Estimates cover one programme family; employee consultation and access work follow GDPR and applicable national rules, with possible additional elapsed waiting.
unknowns: Quality of course objectives and prerequisite metadata.
Whether training access influences promotion, job allocation or continued employment.
Who can approve training time, expenditure and shift changes.
Which employees lack access to the {LMS}.
Applicable collective agreements and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which catalogue and enrolment functions can be configured before writing code?
Can rotating-shift employees participate through repeated sessions or approved asynchronous options?
Does pathway drafting add value beyond structured catalogue filtering?
new_work: Maintain course objectives, prerequisites and capacity rules.
Review proposed pathways and unresolved material gaps.
Handle enrolment conflicts and contested exclusions.
Keep recipient lists and programme notifications accurate.
Check participation barriers and arrange support.
Reassess legal requirements if recommendations are reused for employee evaluation.
tasks.statement: Offer specific training programs to help workers maintain or improve job skills.

tasks.short: Record training participation, monitor progress and evaluate whether programmes improve work.

steps.what: Record attendance, completions and certificates in the learning system.
Export learning records and combine them with role and outcome data.
Check records and calculate participation, completion and outcome measures.
Read learner and manager feedback and summarise recurring concerns.

loop.input: Minimised learner and manager feedback, grouped by programme.
loop.output: Feedback summary with referenced themes and contrary examples.
loop.check: Validate references and theme counts; specialist checks omissions, privacy and unsupported conclusions.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction pass per programme batch; uncertain comments remain uncategorised.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed ratings need no model; open comments use varied language and contain contextual explanations.

steps.what: Interpret results with managers, considering work changes and other explanations.
Approve programme actions and record the evaluation conclusion.

tasks.design: Configure completion recording in the {LMS} and connect approved {HCM} and {OPS_SYSTEM} data through the {DATA_PLATFORM}. The {BI} calculates agreed measures, while a bounded loop summarises feedback into the {DOCS}; people interpret effectiveness and approve programme actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completion reporting was available, but linking learning to work outcomes required manual joins and agreement on meaningful measures.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting features and small integrations can remove compilation work. A bounded loop reduces feedback reading time without claiming causal proof.
tasks.still_hard: Changes in staffing, workload or tools can explain outcome differences. Small groups, missing data and delayed effects limit conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Choose credible measures, challenge causal claims and decide whether a programme deserves investment.

ambition.what: Monthly review of programmes with weak completion or transfer-to-work signals.

tasks.altitude: The specialist replaces recurring export work with investigation of weak signals and conversations with managers. They gain a proposed right to initiate programme reviews, while funding decisions stay with the training manager.

reach.task: Decide which programmes to continue, change or stop.
reach.learn: Evaluation design, uncertainty, opportunity cost and how to present evidence for investment decisions.

evidence.claim: Completion recording, scheduled joins and configured dashboards are established deterministic capabilities; no training-specific case is supplied.
Completion and satisfaction alone do not establish that training caused better work outcomes.
AI intended to monitor or evaluate worker performance can fall within Annex III employment uses; programme-level reporting requires an intended-use assessment.

assumptions: A typical company records completions in the {LMS}, with a spreadsheet bridging outcome sources.
The structured-data prior supports more deterministic automation than the task's overall judgement-heavy label suggests.
Completion recording uses approved criteria and verified attendance, not model-generated competence scores.
Build ranges include access checks, metric validation, a pilot and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; the proposed dashboard evaluates programmes rather than ranking workers.
unknowns: Which outcome measures exist and can lawfully be linked to learning records?
Does the {LMS} receive verified attendance and assessment results automatically?
Are the reports currently used in promotion, discipline or other employment decisions?
Which national consultation rules, retention limits and reporting thresholds apply?
research_questions: Which measures detect transfer to work without introducing excessive employee monitoring?
Can comparison groups or repeated measurements support stronger conclusions for priority programmes?
new_work: Resolve failed joins, disputed completions and missing outcome data.
Review feedback summaries and investigate unusual dashboard results.
Maintain metric definitions, cohort rules, access permissions and intended-use limits.
tasks.statement: Monitor, evaluate, or record training activities or program effectiveness.

tasks.short: Attend meetings and seminars, gather useful ideas, and report training progress.

steps.what: Choose relevant meetings or seminars from invitations and programme priorities.
Prepare programme figures and questions for the selected event.
Attend the event, ask questions, and share relevant training progress.
Turn event notes into a short account of lessons and open questions.

loop.input: Personal event notes and meeting brief.
loop.output: Learning summary with note references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check every factual statement against supplied notes; specialist checks meaning and confidentiality.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; return notes and a blank template if unsupported statements remain.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need interpretation; a template cannot reliably preserve their meaning.

steps.what: Recommend useful follow-ups and send the reviewed summary to management.

tasks.design: A reusable generator combines approved figures from the {LMS} with programme priorities in {DOCS} to prepare a meeting brief. A bounded drafting loop turns personal notes into a source-linked summary in {DOCS}; the specialist reviews it before sharing through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programme figures needed manual assembly, and event notes differed widely. Attendance itself depends on live questions and relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and templates support deterministic preparation. Bounded drafting can reduce note cleanup without requiring automatic recording.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing worthwhile events and judging whether advice fits the workforce remain difficult. Confidential discussions may not be suitable for model processing.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the question nobody prepared, notice disagreement, and judge which lesson deserves action.

ambition.what: A monthly decision on which training module should be refreshed next.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling figures and cleaning notes, while attendance remains substantial. They can bring monthly refresh recommendations; programme approval rights remain with the training manager.

reach.task: Choose programme refresh priorities.
reach.learn: Compare evidence of skill gaps, operational impact, and the cost of changing a module.

evidence.claim: Structured training figures can populate reusable briefs, while free-text notes benefit from reviewed drafting.
Generated reports require source checks; the digest documents a report containing nonexistent references.

assumptions: Time shares describe a typical blend of seminars and programme status meetings, not a mandatory sequence for every event.
Meetings may be remote or in person; personal notes are sufficient and recording is unnecessary.
GDPR applies to personal data in notes; use restricted access, limited retention, and an established lawful basis.
Build ranges cover one brief template, one notes workflow, and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which programme figures are available from the {LMS}?
Which event notes may be processed and shared?
Who can approve programme changes?
What access and employee consultation are required under national rules?
research_questions: Does a brief improve preparation enough to justify its maintenance?
Can summaries preserve caveats and distinguish event claims from verified facts?
new_work: Review summaries for unsupported claims and confidential details.
Maintain figure definitions and brief templates.
Fix broken exports and remove obsolete event notes.
tasks.statement: Attend meetings or seminars to obtain information for use in training programs or to inform management of training program status.

tasks.short: Recruit training participants, resolve placement constraints, and enrol approved cohorts.

steps.what: Collect employee requests and manager nominations for planned training.
Check prerequisites and employee details against training and employee records.
Match eligible requests to course capacity and available dates.
Resolve conflicting priorities, release time, and access needs with participants and managers.
Approve participant release time and proposed placements.
Enrol approved participants and issue session details.

tasks.design: Configure request forms, approvals, enrolment, and reminders in the {LMS} or {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic integration checks limited fields from the {HCM} and {LMS}, then proposes cohorts using capacity and availability; people resolve disputed placements before approved enrolments reach the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived in different formats, employee and course records were separate, and release-time decisions lived in mailboxes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment workflows cover much of the task. Small integrations and explicit scheduling constraints can replace manual copying without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Scarce places, shift coverage, accessibility, and contested development opportunities require discussion. Missing prerequisites need correction rather than automatic exclusion.
tasks.human_edge: Make participation workable and fair when operational demands conflict with an employee's development needs.

ambition.what: Offer recurring training cohorts for shift workers using their actual release windows.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time resolving access barriers and less time chasing nominations. They can propose additional cohort times; managers retain release-time approval.

reach.task: Identify barriers to employee access to development.
reach.learn: Handle sensitive access needs, distinguish missing data from ineligibility, and review participation patterns.

evidence.claim: Forms, explicit prerequisite checks, capacity matching, and enrolment approvals can use deterministic workflows.
AI used for worker evaluation or certain employment decisions can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories.
Dutch national rules include works council consent provisions for specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: Participants are existing employees; this is course recruitment, not hiring.
The {LMS} supports course capacity, enrolment, and completion records.
Checks flag missing records; they do not rank employee potential or decide career opportunities.
GDPR applies; collect only necessary employee fields and restrict sensitive access information.
Build ranges cover one programme family and include applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which prerequisites and allocation priorities are approved?
Does the {LMS} support forms, approvals, and waiting lists?
How are shift coverage and access needs handled?
Which national rules and consultation procedures apply?
Are employee identifiers consistent between the {HCM} and {LMS}?
research_questions: Can existing configuration cover enrolment before custom integration is needed?
Do proposed cohorts improve shift-worker participation without creating coverage gaps?
new_work: Resolve missing records and disputed eligibility checks.
Review waiting-list fairness and unresolved placements.
Maintain capacity, prerequisite, and scheduling rules.
Monitor enrolment failures and duplicate notifications.
tasks.statement: Coordinate recruitment and placement of training program participants.

tasks.short: Review instructor materials for accuracy, learning value, accessibility and fit with agreed objectives.

steps.what: Collect instructor materials, learning objectives and the review checklist.
Check completeness, versions, links and required sections against the checklist.
Assess factual support, instructional sequence, examples and alignment with learning objectives.

loop.input: Versioned instructor materials, learning objectives, checklist and approved reference materials.
loop.output: Suggested findings with page references, supporting passages and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check references exist; the specialist verifies substantive claims and instructional recommendations.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per document, within a fixed page limit; unsupported findings become manual questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules detect missing sections but cannot reliably judge explanations, examples or instructional coherence.

steps.what: Discuss disputed findings and agree revisions with the instructor.
Record the assessment and send revision instructions or acceptance to the instructor.

tasks.design: Configure {DOCS} to assemble versioned review packs, then generate technical checks and a bounded, source-linked quality assessment. The specialist resolves substantive findings with the instructor and approves the recorded assessment before {WORKFLOW} sends it through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical checks were possible, but varied document formats and instructional judgement made a complete review expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls and small validation scripts handle routine checks; bounded text review can prepare evidence-linked findings.
tasks.still_hard: Subject expertise, practical relevance and accessibility beyond mechanical checks remain costly. Missing reference material limits factual verification.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising misleading explanations and knowing what learners will struggle to apply.

ambition.what: A pre-course accessibility and learning-objective review for internally authored courses.

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to learner testing and instructor coaching. Material acceptance remains within existing authority; budget and programme approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Review onboarding guidance before release.
reach.learn: Policy ownership, onboarding requirements and when employment advice needs specialist review.

evidence.claim: Document assembly and mechanical checks can use configuration and deterministic code; these are design estimates.
Instructional quality needs substantive review; the digest provides no demonstrated training-material automation case.
Deloitte partly refunded an Australian government report containing invented sources; this supports source checking, not training-specific performance claims.

assumptions: The baseline represents a mid-size European employer with materials in {DOCS}; time shares are estimates.
Instructors are internal; external correspondence would require separate recipient and disclosure controls.
The specialist can accept routine materials within existing authority.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained: text assistance prepares findings rather than accepting materials.
Build ranges cover one document workflow, accessible files and a limited pilot; consultation delays may extend elapsed time.
GDPR applies if materials contain personal data; national consultation rules vary.
unknowns: Actual document formats, languages and accessibility needs.
Availability and ownership of approved reference materials.
Who may accept materials and send instructor feedback.
Whether materials contain personal or confidential third-party information.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing approvals.
research_questions: Which review criteria can be checked consistently without instructional judgement?
How often does a blinded specialist review reject or materially change suggested findings?
new_work: Verify suggested findings and source passages.
Maintain review criteria and approved references.
Handle unreadable files and conflicting versions.
Sample accepted materials for missed issues.
tasks.statement: Evaluate training materials prepared by instructors, such as outlines, text, or handouts.

tasks.short: Diagnose weak training results, develop alternatives and test a revised approach.

steps.what: Review evaluation evidence for programmes missing expected improvements.
Discuss barriers with learners, instructors and managers.
Develop alternative methods, exercises and pilot designs.

loop.input: Barrier hypotheses, approved materials, method library and capacity limits.
loop.output: Alternative methods and a draft pilot plan with explicit hypotheses and measures.
loop.check: Validate constraints and references; specialist checks pedagogical fit, accessibility and testability.
loop.stop: At most three alternatives and one revision per programme; weak options return to manual design.
loop.why_not_simpler: A method library supplies reusable patterns, but adapting practice to a contextual barrier needs language drafting.

steps.what: Select a method and approve pilot scope, safeguards and measures.
Arrange the approved pilot and coordinate instructors and participants.
Compare pilot outcomes against the agreed baseline and success criteria.
Interpret pilot results and decide whether to revise, expand or stop.

tasks.design: Configure the {BI} to flag missed programme targets and calculate pilot comparisons from approved measures. A bounded loop in the {DOCS} adapts a method library into alternatives, while the {WORKFLOW}, {CALENDAR} and {LMS} coordinate approved pilots; people diagnose barriers and decide adoption.
tasks.previous_blocker: The hard part was contextual diagnosis, not computation. Alternatives were developed from scratch, and small pilots required repeated coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: A reusable method library, deterministic pilot tracking and faster workflow development reduce preparation costs. Bounded drafting helps explore alternatives but does not establish that they will work.
tasks.still_hard: Weak results may come from work conditions rather than teaching methods. Small samples and delayed behaviour change make pilot interpretation expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Form useful hypotheses, design realistic practice and recognise when further training would waste learners' time.

ambition.what: A rapid learning-method pilot service for struggling programmes.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week diagnosing barriers and designing experiments. They gain a proposed mandate to prepare small pilots within an agreed envelope; the training manager approves launch and wider adoption.

reach.task: Address organisational barriers that training cannot resolve.
reach.learn: Change diagnosis, manager accountability and how work design affects skill application.

evidence.claim: Reusable method libraries, pilot workflows and deterministic comparisons can support training redesign.
Drafting alternatives does not demonstrate effectiveness; contextual diagnosis and observed pilot outcomes remain necessary.

assumptions: This models a redesign cycle through pilot evaluation; instructor delivery is separate work.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained in diagnosis and adoption, while preparation and pilot administration remain open to change.
Scheduling and enrolment stay within the approved pilot plan; deviations become exceptions.
Build ranges assume reuse of the evaluation data pipeline and exclude the elapsed time needed to observe learning outcomes.
Access and consultation ranges include employee consultation under applicable national rules where pilot participation or data use changes.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; pilot comparisons do not automatically trigger individual employment decisions.
unknowns: Is there an approved method library and a reliable baseline?
Who can authorise pilot time, budget and participation?
How long must outcomes be observed before a useful comparison is possible?
Which national consultation rules and learner-data permissions apply?
research_questions: Which pilot designs can distinguish a teaching-method problem from lack of workplace opportunity?
Can alternatives be tested without disadvantaging participants or withholding required training?
new_work: Review drafted methods and remove unsupported assumptions.
Maintain the method library, pilot templates and success criteria.
Handle scheduling exceptions, monitor pilot execution and document uncertain results.
tasks.statement: Develop alternative training methods if expected improvements are not seen.

tasks.short: Assess learning needs through surveys, interviews and consultation, then agree training priorities.

steps.what: Agree the assessment scope with managers.
Prepare survey questions and interview prompts.

loop.input: Assessment scope and approved question bank.
loop.output: Assessment questions linked to the scope.
loop.check: Check scope coverage and prohibited questions; specialist checks neutrality, accessibility and relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per assessment; unresolved issues return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse approved questions first; a bounded loop adapts wording to unfamiliar learning needs.

steps.what: Send the survey and collect responses through a form.
Interview employees and facilitate focus groups about work barriers.
Combine survey results with role and training records.
Summarise recurring needs and distinguish training gaps from other barriers.

loop.input: Minimised survey text, consultation notes and aggregate needs dataset.
loop.output: Needs brief with source references, themes and unresolved explanations.
loop.check: Validate references and counts; specialist checks minority views and training versus process explanations.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass per batch; ambiguous themes remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Counts are deterministic, but varied descriptions of work barriers require interpreting free text.

steps.what: Agree priorities, owners and non-training referrals with managers.

tasks.design: Configure assessment forms and reminders in the {WORKFLOW}, then join permitted {HCM} and {LMS} records on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Bounded loops prepare questions and a referenced needs brief in the {DOCS}; the specialist conducts consultations and managers approve priorities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms already handled collection, but records used different identifiers and interpreting work barriers required context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, configurable forms and faster integration development make the plumbing cheaper. Bounded text processing can prepare material for review without settling priorities.
tasks.still_hard: Employees may withhold sensitive concerns. Training gaps can resemble poor tools, workload problems or unclear management expectations.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, probe contradictions and recognise when a training request masks a different problem.

ambition.what: A work-barrier diagnostic that routes process problems to HR and managers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time compiling responses and more time testing explanations with employees. They gain a proposed referral mandate; managers still decide resources and priorities.

reach.task: Investigate recurring employee concerns behind training requests.
reach.learn: Confidential intake, referral thresholds and how to distinguish individual concerns from organisational patterns.

evidence.claim: Configurable forms, record joins and bounded text summaries can support training-needs assessment; this is a design estimate.
Trust-building and separating learning needs from work-design problems usually require human consultation.

assumptions: This describes a typical mixed workflow, not a confirmed customer process.
The time split follows the consultation-heavy prior; a mailbox is not assumed to be the main intake channel.
Survey sending uses an approved internal audience and question set.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and include access, privacy review and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; identifiable responses are minimised and access restricted.
unknowns: Which forms, identifiers and export permissions are available?
Are surveys anonymous, confidential or attributable, and what reporting group sizes are permitted?
Which national consultation rules and existing employee agreements apply?
Can the specialist refer non-training problems directly to HR or managers?
research_questions: How reliably can reviewed themes distinguish skill gaps from process barriers?
Does the question bank cover the languages and accessibility needs of participants?
new_work: Review drafted questions and source-linked themes.
Handle missing identifiers and suppress unsafe reporting groups.
Maintain the question bank, referral categories, access controls and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Assess training needs through surveys, interviews with employees, focus groups, or consultation with managers, instructors, or customer representatives.

tasks.short: Select suitable instructors, agree availability, and record training assignments.

steps.what: Translate learning objectives and cohort needs into instructor requirements.
Check instructor qualifications, approved rates, and availability.
Compare instructors against required qualifications, dates, language, and budget.
Select an instructor using subject expertise, teaching approach, and cohort fit.
Agree session dates and delivery expectations with the selected instructor.
Record the confirmed assignment and update session invitations.

tasks.design: Generate instructor requirements from a structured training brief in {DOCS}, then join approved instructor records, rates, and availability from the {LMS}, {PROCUREMENT}, and {CALENDAR}. A deterministic shortlist exposes constraints and missing data; the specialist selects the instructor, agrees delivery expectations, and triggers configured assignment updates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructor qualifications, rates, and calendars were maintained separately. Teaching fit was mixed into administrative comparisons.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable schemas and small integrations can assemble reliable comparisons quickly. Explicit filters handle administrative requirements without automated teaching-quality scores.
tasks.still_hard: Availability can be stale, and qualifications do not prove teaching quality. New instructors and unusual cohorts need direct assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise whether an instructor can teach this audience and establish clear expectations before delivery.

ambition.what: Maintain a qualified backup instructor option for critical onboarding sessions.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling shortlists and more time assessing teaching fit and delivery resilience. Selection rights remain within the existing budget and delegation limits.

reach.task: Plan instructor capacity for critical programmes.
reach.learn: Assess coverage risk, teaching quality, and the cost of retaining backup capacity.

evidence.claim: Qualification, availability, and budget constraints support deterministic shortlisting while teaching fit remains a human decision.
AI-based worker evaluation or task allocation can raise EU AI Act high-risk questions depending on purpose.

assumptions: The training brief contains structured objectives, language, delivery mode, and required qualifications.
External instructors already have approved commercial terms; new contracting follows a separate approval process.
The specialist has delegated authority to choose instructors within approved limits.
GDPR applies to instructor records; use limited fields, access controls, and correction procedures.
Build ranges include consultation under national rules where employee assignment or monitoring arrangements change.
unknowns: Where are instructor qualifications and expiry dates recorded?
Which filters are mandatory and which allow exceptions?
Who approves external instructor bookings and additional spend?
How reliable are instructor calendars?
What employee consultation is required under national rules?
research_questions: Can the {LMS} already store instructor qualifications and resource availability?
Does a deterministic shortlist retain suitable instructors when records are incomplete?
new_work: Keep instructor qualifications, rates, and availability current.
Resolve missing records and justified filter exceptions.
Check assignment updates and calendar conflicts.
Review backup coverage and instructor feedback.
tasks.statement: Select and assign instructors to conduct training.

tasks.short: Design leadership development programmes for employees progressing towards management and executive roles.

steps.what: Gather role requirements, existing programmes and aggregated development needs.
Agree target roles, learning outcomes and programme constraints with sponsors.
Design learning modules, practice assignments, mentoring and evaluation methods.

loop.input: Agreed outcomes, budget and time constraints, approved learning resources and programme templates.
loop.output: Draft programme with outcome-to-activity mapping, practice assignments and evaluation options.
loop.check: Validate schedule and cost constraints in code; the specialist verifies learning design and references.
loop.stop: Produce at most two options and one revision each; unresolved design choices return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the plan but cannot adapt practice scenarios and learning sequences to varied leadership needs.

steps.what: Test programme relevance with subject experts, line managers and prospective learners.
Approve the pilot plan, resources and participant list.
Set up the approved programme, enrol participants and schedule sessions.

tasks.design: Assemble an aggregate development brief from {DOCS} and authorised {TALENT} records, then use a bounded drafting loop to populate programme templates in {DOCS}. People agree outcomes, validate learning design and approve participation; configured {LMS} and {CALENDAR} workflows launch the approved pilot.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leadership development depends on organisational context, sponsor commitment and suitable practice opportunities; templates solved only part of the work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable document assembly, constraint checks and bounded drafting make programme options cheaper to prepare without predicting executive potential.
tasks.still_hard: Fair access, manager support and measuring transfer to real work remain difficult. Individual worker evaluation or career-affecting recommendations require separate GDPR and EU AI Act assessment; relevant scope appears in [S17] and [S20].
tasks.human_edge: Designing credible stretch opportunities and securing managers' commitment to let employees practise.

ambition.what: A first-line leadership pilot for shift-based employees who cannot attend standard daytime programmes.

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to designing workplace practice and negotiating access for overlooked groups. The specialist can prepare more programme options; participant selection and budget rights remain with authorised managers.

reach.task: Plan internal management-development pathways.
reach.learn: Succession governance, fair nomination processes and boundaries between development and promotion decisions.

evidence.claim: Programme templates, resource assembly and enrolment can use deterministic tools; contextual drafting can use a bounded model loop.
Leadership programme quality and workplace transfer require human validation; the digest contains no relevant outcome case.

assumptions: The baseline combines document design, sponsor discussions and existing {LMS} administration.
The judgement and relationship priors outweigh the task's automation probability for programme choices.
The solution does not score executive potential, rank employees or recommend promotion.
Development needs are aggregated, with suppression where small groups could identify individuals.
The training manager has delegated pilot approval authority.
Build ranges cover the preparation workflow and pilot setup, not delivery or long-term effectiveness evaluation.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national employment and employee consultation rules vary.
unknowns: Existing nomination and participant approval processes.
Whether development records may be reused for programme planning.
Leadership framework, target roles and available practice assignments.
Budget authority, manager availability and shift coverage.
Applicable consultation requirements and employee representation.
Whether intended use extends into individual worker evaluation.
research_questions: Which programme elements require local workplace practice rather than course content?
What pilot measures distinguish course satisfaction from changed workplace behaviour?
Which scheduling and nomination barriers exclude shift-based employees?
new_work: Verify draft activities, references and outcome alignment.
Maintain approved programme resources and constraint templates.
Check aggregate data for disclosure risks.
Handle enrolment and scheduling exceptions.
Gather pilot feedback and revise practice assignments.
tasks.statement: Devise programs to develop executive potential among employees in lower-level positions.

tasks.short: Negotiate training scope, outcomes, fees, and expenses, then secure an approved contract.

steps.what: Discuss the client's training needs, intended outcomes, and delivery constraints.
Calculate delivery costs, proposed fees, expense limits, and permitted concessions.
Draft contract terms using approved clauses and the proposed delivery scope.

loop.input: Training brief, validated cost proposal, and approved clause library.
loop.output: Draft scope and outcome wording within a deterministically populated agreement.
loop.check: Validate amounts and required clauses mechanically; specialist checks scope, commitments, and source references.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved wording returns to the specialist. Never send automatically.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill prices and standard clauses, but bespoke training outcomes require reviewed free-text drafting.

steps.what: Negotiate outcomes, scope, fees, and expenses within delegated limits.
Review nonstandard clauses and resolve legal or liability concerns.
Approve the final commitments and sign through the authorised signing process.
File the signed agreement and register delivery obligations and billing details.

tasks.design: Configure cost formulas using approved rates from the {ERP}, and populate standard terms in the {CLM}. A bounded loop drafts only bespoke scope wording for review; people negotiate and authorise commitments through {ESIGN}, after which a deterministic integration registers obligations in {PROJECT} and billing details in the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scope, price assumptions, and contract versions were scattered across documents. Bespoke outcomes and negotiation could not be reduced to templates alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates, formulas, approval routes, and signing workflows cover the structured work. Bounded drafting can help with bespoke wording when approved inputs are available.
tasks.still_hard: Outcome commitments, liability, scope changes, and concessions need judgement. Contract integrations are expensive when signed documents do not retain structured fields.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what the client truly values, trade concessions wisely, and avoid promises the training programme cannot deliver.
tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time rebuilding cost sheets and contract paperwork, with more preparation time for negotiation. Negotiation limits and signing rights do not change.

reach.task: Approve training commitments against workforce priorities and budget.
reach.learn: Define measurable outcomes, understand contract exposure, and distinguish delivery commitments from guaranteed performance gains.

evidence.claim: Cost formulas, standard contract assembly, approval routing, and obligation registration can be deterministic.
Bespoke contract drafting needs source verification and human review before external use.

assumptions: This task applies where the company provides training to external clients; many internal HR teams rarely perform it.
Approved rates, clauses, and delegation limits exist.
Legal review focuses on deviations; routine agreements may follow a shorter approved route.
GDPR applies to personal data exchanged during contracting; national rules govern relevant employment and consultation matters.
Build ranges cover one contract family and include access, legal template review, and applicable employee consultation.
unknowns: Does the role negotiate external client contracts or only internal training agreements?
Which commitments can the specialist make without further approval?
Are approved clauses and pricing rules maintained?
Can the {CLM} and {ESIGN} preserve structured contract fields?
Which employee consultation and access procedures apply under national rules?
research_questions: How much contract wording is genuinely bespoke after templates are standardised?
Can obligations be transferred from approved structured fields without interpreting signed documents?
new_work: Review generated scope wording and detect commitments beyond the brief.
Maintain approved rates, clauses, and delegation limits.
Resolve contract-version mismatches and failed obligation transfers.
Check that registered billing and delivery details match the signed agreement.
tasks.statement: Negotiate contracts with clients for desired training outcomes, fees, or expenses.

tasks.short: Help trainees find appropriate employment, placement, or social support and arrange agreed referrals.

steps.what: Discuss the trainee's needs, preferences, and immediate support concerns privately.
Clarify internal support routes and any employment-process boundaries.
Look up suitable internal contacts and verified external support services.
Discuss options and choose whether to proceed and what information may be shared.
Prepare and send the agreed introduction with only necessary details.
Record referral status and arrange a discreet follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure a maintained service directory in the {DOCS} with filters for location, service type, and published eligibility. A template generator prepares a minimal introduction in the {EMAIL}; the trainee approves its recipient and contents before sending. Configured flows keep a restricted status record in the {HCM} and arrange follow-up through the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Referral knowledge sat with individual staff, and service details changed. Personal circumstances and privacy made automatic referral decisions unsuitable.
tasks.enabler_now: Directory configuration, templates, and restricted workflows can remove lookup and administration effort. None requires a model to interpret sensitive disclosures.
tasks.still_hard: Services may have waiting lists or unclear eligibility. The specialist must recognise limits to their competence and choose appropriate escalation. GDPR lawful basis and any special-category conditions need assessment; trainee permission to share is not a blanket lawful basis for employee data processing.
tasks.human_edge: Build enough trust for the trainee to express what help they want, without pressure or unnecessary disclosure.

ambition.what: Offer a confidential support-navigation appointment to trainees approaching an employment transition.

tasks.altitude: The week still centres on private conversations and careful coordination, with less directory searching and referral administration. No new authority over trainee choices or external service eligibility is gained.

reach.task: Coordinate an employment transition with suitable support.
reach.learn: Distinguish support navigation from employment decisions and understand escalation routes.

reach.task: Check whether trainees can access support fairly.
reach.learn: Assess language, disability, location, and eligibility barriers without building unnecessary personal profiles.

evidence.claim: A verified directory, template introduction, and restricted status workflow can reduce administration while leaving referral judgement and conversations human.
For a mid-size European employer, this supplemental task commonly maps to internal support or external transition services; its actual scope varies.

assumptions: This task occurs when trainee support needs arise; it is not a general social-service case-management function.
The organisation permits referrals and has a defined escalation route.
The directory filters published service facts and does not infer vulnerability or decide eligibility.
The trainee can choose self-referral instead of an employer introduction.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates, including privacy review, access, and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Whether the employer provides this service and which trainees it covers.
Available internal contacts, service directories, and escalation arrangements.
The lawful basis, retention period, and permitted content of referral records.
Whether the {HCM} supports sufficiently restricted records.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Who verifies service availability and eligibility information, and how often?
Can the process record status without retaining sensitive circumstances?
Would trainees prefer direct contact details to an employer-mediated introduction?
new_work: Verify service contacts, eligibility details, and directory expiry dates.
Check introduction contents and capture approval before external sharing.
Handle unavailable services, declined referrals, and safeguarding escalations.
Audit record access and remove records when retention periods expire.
tasks.statement: Refer trainees to employer relations representatives, to locations offering job placement assistance, or to appropriate social services agencies, if warranted.

tasks.short: Develop and deliver practical training on resource efficiency, recycling, and environmental procedures.

steps.what: Agree target behaviours, affected roles, and operational constraints with the environmental specialist.
Collect approved procedures, site instructions, and relevant operational examples.
Write learning objectives, examples, exercises, and knowledge checks.

loop.input: Training brief, approved procedures, site instructions, and course template.
loop.output: Draft objectives, exercises, facilitator notes, and answer keys linked to source passages.
loop.check: Validate required sections and source references; specialist checks pedagogy and answer keys. Flag missing guidance rather than invent it.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported instructions or unresolved contradictions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise material, but adapting prose and exercises to different roles requires bounded writing.

steps.what: Check technical accuracy and approve environmental instructions for release.
Publish the approved module and assign the relevant learner groups.
Deliver practical demonstrations and discuss site-specific questions with learners.
Record attendance and knowledge-check results.
Review completion, learner questions, and operational measures to identify training changes.

tasks.design: Versioned procedures in the {DOCS} feed a course template and bounded drafting loop, with technical approval before release. Configured flows publish approved modules and record completions in the {LMS}, using class bookings from the scheduling workflow. A deterministic {BI} view combines completion totals with site-level environmental measures to support improvement discussions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing role-specific material required substantial writing and technical review. Procedures, completion records, and environmental measures were not linked.
tasks.enabler_now: Source metadata, reusable course templates, and bounded drafting reduce preparation effort. Existing publishing features and small deterministic integrations connect delivery records with operational measures.
tasks.still_hard: Local waste handling and efficiency procedures vary by site. Technical claims need expert approval, and operational improvements cannot automatically be attributed to training. Hands-on behaviour change still needs demonstration and reinforcement.
tasks.human_edge: Translate environmental procedures into realistic workplace habits and recognise when equipment, incentives, or workflow prevent learners from applying them.

ambition.what: Provide short shift-based environmental training for temporary staff who miss scheduled classroom sessions.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time collecting sources, drafting repeated material, and entering completions. They can recommend targeted refresher sessions sooner; environmental policy and site operating decisions remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Choose between refresher training and a broader programme redesign.
reach.learn: Interpret completion and operational measures without claiming unsupported causation.

reach.task: Include temporary and shift staff in induction.
reach.learn: Map role requirements, language needs, access arrangements, and paid learning time.

evidence.claim: Templates, bounded source-based drafting, configured publishing, and deterministic reporting can support course development; the digest contains no direct training-product case.
The digest documents an Australian government report containing nonexistent sources, supporting explicit citation checks for generated training material.
Completion and site-level outcome trends support investigation but do not establish that training caused operational changes.

assumptions: An environmental specialist can approve site procedures and technical instructions.
Training uses approved local procedures rather than generated legal interpretations.
Attendance comes from learner check-in or a confirmed roster; successful completion uses defined knowledge-check rules.
Operational reporting uses site-level measures and avoids individual worker scoring.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates, including access and applicable national employee consultation.
unknowns: Which procedures are current, approved, and available in usable formats.
Whether course publication and attendance capture can be configured in the {LMS}.
Availability and quality of site-level environmental measures.
Temporary staff access, language needs, and time allowed for training.
Applicable consultation arrangements and permitted links between learning and operational data.
research_questions: Which training topics require practical demonstration rather than a self-service module?
How much expert correction do generated exercises and answer keys require?
Which operational measures are useful without introducing individual employee monitoring?
new_work: Verify source references, exercises, and answer keys.
Maintain course templates and approved source versions.
Trigger review when an underlying procedure changes.
Resolve missing attendance and completion records.
Investigate outcome trends with site owners and distinguish training gaps from operational barriers.
tasks.statement: Develop or implement training programs related to efficiency, recycling, or other issues with environmental impacts.

tasks.short: Compare training delivery options using learning outcomes, costs, accessibility and environmental estimates.

steps.what: Export attendance, completion and assessment results from the {LMS}.
Collect course costs, travel assumptions and participant feedback from finance and course owners.
Reconcile cohorts and calculate delivery costs and environmental estimates in {SPREADSHEET}.
Read comments and summarise delivery barriers and learner preferences in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Minimised participant comments and an approved delivery-barrier taxonomy.
loop.output: Feedback themes with supporting comment references and unresolved items.
loop.check: Validate references and categories; the specialist checks themes and minority concerns before use.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass; unclear comments remain unclassified for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Attendance and costs are structured, but free-text descriptions of barriers need language interpretation.

steps.what: Discuss effectiveness, accessibility and operational constraints with line managers and course owners.
Document a delivery recommendation and proposed pilot in {DOCS}.
Approve the pilot's delivery mode, budget and success criteria.

tasks.design: Scheduled connectors bring course outcomes from the {LMS} and costs from the {ERP} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}; configured forms in {WORKFLOW} collect missing feedback and travel assumptions. Deterministic calculations feed a {BI} comparison, while a bounded loop summarises comments and a template produces the recommendation; the training and development manager approves each pilot.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course, cost and feedback records used different identifiers. Comparing delivery modes also required assumptions that were rarely recorded consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Small connectors and reusable calculation rules can now be built more cheaply. Free-text classification supports the comparison without turning it into an automated delivery decision.
tasks.still_hard: Different cohorts and assessments make causal comparisons difficult. Environmental estimates depend on travel and energy assumptions; dashboards cannot establish that one mode caused better learning.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist distinguishes poor delivery from unsuitable content, operational disruption and differences between learner groups.

ambition.what: A monthly delivery-mode review for courses with comparable outcome data.

tasks.altitude: The specialist replaces occasional spreadsheet assembly with regular evidence reviews and pilot follow-up. They can recommend changes more often; budget and delivery approval stay with the training and development manager.

reach.task: Allocate training budget between delivery formats.
reach.learn: Budget authority, opportunity costs and acceptable evidence for changing delivery.

reach.task: Review whether training access differs across employee groups.
reach.learn: Privacy-preserving comparisons, accessibility obligations and limits of small samples.

evidence.claim: Cost calculations, cohort reconciliation and delivery dashboards can use deterministic rules.
Observed training outcomes alone do not establish causal differences between delivery modes.
The GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
The digest identifies works council consent requirements for certain HR data and monitoring arrangements in the Netherlands.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
Evaluation concerns courses and cohorts rather than individual employment decisions.
Course identifiers can be mapped across the {LMS} and {ERP}.
Environmental factors and calculation boundaries will be explicitly approved and recorded.
Estimates cover a limited course portfolio and existing reporting infrastructure.
Consent and access effort includes GDPR review, employee consultation where national rules apply, and checking whether a DPIA is required; elapsed consultation may take longer.
unknowns: Availability of comparable assessment results and sufficiently sized cohorts.
Whether course costs include staff time, travel and facilities.
Availability and quality of environmental calculation factors.
Whether feedback is identifiable and how it may be reused.
Applicable national consultation rules and permitted reporting granularity.
research_questions: Which courses support a credible comparison or controlled delivery pilot?
Which missing costs could change the delivery recommendation?
Can reporting meet evaluation needs using aggregated data?
new_work: Maintain course mappings and cost assumptions.
Review failed reconciliations and missing inputs.
Check feedback themes for omitted accessibility concerns.
Follow up pilots and distinguish correlation from evidence of improvement.
Maintain access controls and reporting suppression rules.
tasks.statement: Evaluate modes of training delivery, such as in-person or virtual, to optimize training effectiveness, training costs, or environmental impacts.

tasks.short: Design orientation and training programmes, prepare materials and organise delivery.

steps.what: Agree learner outcomes, audience and delivery constraints with stakeholders.
Design the learning sequence, practice activities and assessment approach.
Draft learning materials, exercises and facilitator guidance.

loop.input: Programme plan, approved source material and selected templates.
loop.output: Draft learning materials with source references and labelled gaps.
loop.check: Check required sections and source references; specialist reviews learning alignment, accessibility and examples.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per module; missing facts become questions for the expert.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but adapting explanations and practice scenarios requires bounded language generation.

steps.what: Validate technical accuracy and approve the learning materials.
Coordinate instructors, rooms and dates through messages and calendar checks.
Publish approved courses and enrol the agreed employee audience.
Brief instructors and decide whether the programme is ready to start.

tasks.design: Use approved templates in the {DOCS} and a bounded drafting loop to produce materials from a human-designed programme plan. A scheduling workflow checks the {CALENDAR}, and configured {LMS} rules publish approved content and enrol agreed audiences after content and schedule approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reusable templates existed, but adapting materials took time and scheduling crossed documents, messages and learning records.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster development makes small scheduling and publishing connections economical. Source-constrained drafting can prepare materials for specialist and expert review.
tasks.still_hard: Good learning design depends on realistic practice and learner context. Technical accuracy, accessibility and customer-specific obligations still need accountable review.
tasks.human_edge: Design practice that changes behaviour and judge whether learners can use it in their actual work.
tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time designing practice and briefing instructors, with less document assembly and scheduling. They gain a proposed right to adapt activities within approved outcomes and budget.

reach.task: Coordinate new-starter orientation and track readiness.
reach.learn: Joiner triggers, role eligibility, enrolment exceptions and the handoff from orientation to workplace practice.

evidence.claim: Template generators, constraint-based scheduling and configured enrolment can reduce programme administration.
Bounded drafting can adapt approved material, but instructional quality and technical correctness need review.

assumptions: The steps describe employee programmes; customer delivery requires an explicit external audience and publishing policy.
Creation and consultation dominate the time split, consistent with the priors; scheduling messages are a smaller component.
The expert can approve content, and the specialist can approve schedules within an existing budget.
Build ranges cover a reusable pilot workflow, not the creation of an entire course library.
Access and consultation ranges include national employee consultation where audience assignment or employee-data use changes.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; source material and learner data use approved access and retention settings.
unknowns: Which course templates, content formats and publishing interfaces are supported?
Who approves content, enrolment criteria and customer-facing publication?
Are instructors and rooms represented consistently in the {CALENDAR}?
Which languages, accessibility requirements and national consultation rules apply?
research_questions: Which modules can use existing approved materials without substantial rewriting?
Can the publishing workflow preserve accessible formats and course version history?
new_work: Review generated explanations, exercises and source references.
Handle scheduling conflicts and enrolment exceptions.
Maintain approved sources, templates, publishing rules and accessibility checks.
tasks.statement: Design, plan, organize, or direct orientation and training programs for employees or customers.

tasks.short: Collect approved sources and develop accurate, usable course materials and training guides.

steps.what: Find procedures, existing guides and approved templates in {DOCS}.
Ask the subject expert to resolve missing or conflicting source instructions.
Confirm current procedures and explain exceptions in response to the clarification request.
Draft explanations, examples, exercises and answer keys in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved source bundle, source clarification, learning objectives and content templates.
loop.output: Course draft with source references, exercises and proposed answer keys.
loop.check: Validate references, required sections and objective coverage; route substantive content to expert review.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted correction passes; unresolved gaps remain flagged for manual authoring.
loop.why_not_simpler: Formatting is deterministic, but explaining procedures and creating useful exercises requires writing.

steps.what: Review technical accuracy, examples and answer keys; approve or request changes.
Format approved content into guides, handouts and visual materials in {DOCS}.
Check accessibility and release the versioned course pack through the {LMS}.

tasks.design: A deterministic connector retrieves current approved sources from {DOCS}, and a bounded drafting loop produces referenced course content. Template code creates the course pack; configured approvals in {WORKFLOW} require expert content approval and a training specialist's release check before publication to the {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source versions were scattered, and each course needed fresh writing and manual formatting. Expert clarification could not be replaced by document assembly.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes source connectors and reusable generators cheaper to build. Bounded drafting can use approved material while leaving technical approval with the subject expert.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting procedures, safety-critical explanations, accessibility and specialist review remain costly. The automation prior overstates how much expert validation can disappear.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist knows where learners misunderstand a procedure; the subject expert decides which explanation is technically safe.

ambition.what: A procedure-change learning bulletin with a short practice exercise.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling files and more time testing explanations with learners. Content release remains within existing approval rights.

reach.task: Update onboarding guidance when employee policies change.
reach.learn: Policy approval history, effective dates and employee-facing wording.

reach.task: Prioritise course revisions across the training catalogue.
reach.learn: Content risk, revision backlog and the effect of procedure changes on learning objectives.

evidence.claim: Source retrieval, template rendering and versioned publishing can use deterministic software.
Drafting course explanations from approved sources is feasible, but learning quality requires review and learner testing.
The digest documents a report containing nonexistent sources, supporting explicit reference checks.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
Shares include active expert review time across the task, excluding waiting for replies.
Approved procedures have stable identifiers and accessible version metadata.
The first release covers one course family and existing material templates.
Draft generation time is removed from the person; expert review remains a separate step.
Access estimates include source permissions and employee consultation where national rules apply; calendar delays may exceed working effort.
unknowns: How approved procedure versions are distinguished from drafts.
Which course materials require safety, legal or regulatory approval.
Existing accessibility requirements and supported output formats.
Availability of subject experts and rights to reuse source materials.
Whether learner examples contain personal data.
research_questions: Can approved source versions be retrieved reliably without semantic search?
Which errors survive reference checks and require expert judgement?
Do learners understand generated explanations as well as current materials?
new_work: Review technical accuracy and answer keys.
Resolve missing or conflicting sources.
Maintain templates, source mappings and drafting instructions.
Test rendered accessibility and retire outdated course versions.
Collect learner feedback on revised explanations.
tasks.statement: Obtain, organize, or develop training procedure manuals, guides, or course materials, such as handouts or visual materials.

tasks.short: Track training spending and commitments, explain variances and prepare budget reports.

steps.what: Provide posted training costs by account, cost centre and reporting period.
Provide open purchase commitments for training suppliers and programmes.
Export enrolments and completions for the reporting period.
